sections.title: The dashboard
items: The home page at smcmurry6-source.github.io/study-hubs. Bookmark this, not individual hubs. It was redrawn in November 2026: same address, and your progress, rank, trophies and settings came with you.

Guided tour: A short walk through the dashboard on the real page, ten stops at most. It no longer asks on your first visit. Take the tour in the top bar's menu (the three lines). Each hub has its own tour too.

Your hubs: Every live hub is a tab along the top with its emblem and its exam's countdown, soonest first, the open one in the hub's color. The page opens on the hub whose exam is next, or the one you had open last. The open hub shows its drawn scene across the page, the exam's date, the days left on a tile that flips like a departure board, a bead for each day left (up to two weeks out, ending on the hub's emblem), the hub's other exams, a ring for your progress in it (questions tried, how many right), and Start studying and Daily drill with today's status. Along its bottom: the hub's Timmy Time episode when it has one, with Timmy on the air in his headphones, and Send luck the day before an exam. What's new is the box under it: the latest changes to that hub and to every hub as cards on a timeline, newest first and biggest, each with when it happened and which hub it's for. Swipe it (or use its arrows) for older ones. Tap More on a long one. Changes since your last visit say New, with a count at the top; this device remembers what you've seen. About this hub, at its top, opens what the hub covers. A hub archives itself at 10 pm on its last exam day and moves to Past hubs at the bottom for 10 days.

Send luck: The day before an exam and the morning of it (until 2 pm), a tile at the bottom of the hub's card, beside Timmy Time, has a big green Send luck button with a lucky clover (it turns gold once you've sent yours, one per exam). It shows how many classmates sent it and the latest names.

You: One card for everything that's yours: the name classmates see, with Pick your name / Change name (everyone starts with a random class name like "Gleaming Molar"); Timmy at his place, in what you put on him; your rank as the card's centerpiece, on dark plum with gold rays turning behind the medallion: its name, your XP counting up, your place in the class, a gold bar to the next level with the next medallion waiting at its end, your mastery medals, and buttons for the Trophy case and The road ahead; your Shiny Gold Crowns with Timmy's Shop and your Collections; your day streak with the last seven days as dots; and this week's answers with a ring for how many were right. The top bar shows your streak and rank too. The road, under the boards: the three journeys one under the other (Handpiece, ModuPro, Loupes), each opening to its seven ranks on a track that fills in gold as far as you've come, with the XP each rank starts at and its levels I, II and III. Yours is open and marked "You are here"; tap a later journey to see what's waiting.

The class: Studying right now is a drawn classroom: the count on the chalkboard with how many are in each hub, and a Timmy at a desk for everyone who has a hub open, wearing the outfit on at their own Timmy's place (a plain tooth when nothing is on, or with Timmy or the extras off). When someone opens a hub their Timmy hops in through the door and jumps into a desk; when they close it he gets up and leaves. The desk's front is the hub's color, the windows show day or night, rows are added as the room fills, and past a full room a sign by the door says how many are in the hall. No names: nobody can tell which Timmy is anyone else's. Your own Timmy's desk has a "You" plate while you have a hub open in another tab, on your screen only. Reduced motion (or answer animations off) seats them without the walk; Focus mode shows the plain count. The count is in the top bar too. Under it, the leaderboard, one list at a time: Ranks (the top 10, with every rank from Stone to Dark Matter folded under it) or Study streaks, with the top three on a stage: curtains, spotlights, confetti, gold, silver and bronze blocks, a crown for first, and each winner's own Timmy on top in their outfit. Mastery medals show next to every name. Tap anyone to visit their Timmy's place. Today's Golden Probe winner is under the board when there is one. Correct-in-a-row, the arcade high scores (each hub's Arcade keeps its own boards) and the "When people study" chart are no longer on the dashboard.

Idea board: A cork board where every idea is a pinned note: the paper's color and the little picture say what kind it is, the pushpin is in its hub's color (red for all hubs), Sam's answer is stamped on it and the top idea wears a rosette. Post an idea for the hubs and vote on your classmates'. An idea has a title and up to 280 characters, the hub it's for (or all hubs) and what kind it is: a new feature, making something work better, questions and notes, games and fun, look and feel, or something else. It shows to the class right away under your leaderboard name, with its up and down votes. One vote per idea; tap again to take it back. Top, New and Shipped tabs, and filters by hub and by kind. Three ideas a day. Report hides an idea after three reports until Sam looks; you can delete your own, and its votes go with it. Sam marks ideas Under consideration, Planned, Shipped or Not doing with a line on why, and you get that in your Inbox if it's yours or you voted it up. Votes show what the class wants; they don't decide what gets built. No quiz or exam questions or answers, and nothing about a classmate. Its own section on the dashboard; in a hub, under More.

Past hubs: Each finished exam's recap is a drawn card in that hub's color, one exam at a time (chips switch between them): the hours studied together, the classmates as a crowd of teeth, hours per day as a bar graph (the exam day's column with a flag, the most hours labeled, Timmy standing on one), then chips for how many answers were right, the day before the exam, the busiest hour, night owls and regulars, and "the one that got us" when there is one. The numbers count up and the columns grow as you reach it. Save image still gives the shareable picture. Totals only, no names. Above it, Exam check-ins: every check-in still open for a closed hub in one place, each with its exam date and a Check in button, and "Sent" once you've done it.

Exam check-ins: From 8 am on exam day (or once the exam closes, for an exam open all day, like PCD Exam 3 until 8 pm) a "Check in" button appears on the hub card; from 10 pm a pop-up asks once. Short questions: how ready you felt, how it went, how the hub compared to the exam, and what the hub could have done better (Occlusion's midterm also asks how helpful the diagrams and the picture Patient Box questions were; PCD Implants also asks whether its new drawn Patient Box cases were better than the Patient Box questions you had before and how helpful its diagrams were, each with an "I didn't use them" button that keeps those who skipped them out of the rating, which of its study tools helped you (tick any), and how it felt that the hub kept changing up to exam day). Please don't write out exam questions or answers, since the honor code keeps exam content private. The answers shape the next hubs. Your first check-in for each exam earns +1,000 XP and +1,000 Shiny Gold Crowns (checking in again later is welcome, but pays once). The button is under the open hub from 8 am on exam day, and in the Exam check-ins panel at the top of Past hubs once it archives (every closed hub's open check-in together); the 10 pm pop-up is unchanged, and it waits while a reply to one of your reports is on screen. Under "What could the hub have done better?" a box, ticked to start, also posts that answer on the idea board under your leaderboard name. You see the post first (its title, text and kind, all yours to change); untick it and the answer goes only to Sam, as before. Your other answers are never posted. The check-in opens in a window in the middle of the screen with Timmy peeking over its top edge (in whatever he's wearing at his place) and a line for each step, and a bar that fills toward a crown as you go. Send it and the thank-you celebrates: a gold sunburst, confetti and crowns, your XP and crowns counting up, and Timmy jumping for joy. Tap Collect and they fly into your rank at the top of the page. With reduced motion or "Answer animations" off, it's all still. Said "Not now"? Now and then a check-in you skipped asks once more, never twice. A check-in stays open for a while after its exam, then closes as newer exams come (Sam closes the older ones): its button and pop-up go, and it can't be sent any more. What you already sent is kept.
Inbox: Replies to your reports and suggestions (kept 90 days) and notices to the whole class (60 days). The top-bar button shows an unread count; new items pop up once in the bottom right.

Settings and theme: The gear opens Settings: Theme, Text size, Focus mode (the same switch as in a hub: no streak, XP, ranks, boards or Timmy), and the extras (Timmy, hidden secrets, plaque bosses, the Tooth Fairy, the Golden Probe, tactical nukes, rank-up and trophy cards, streak cheers, the streak flame, answer animations). Light or dark is also in the top bar's menu. Font, Background sound and Accent are gone: the redesign has one typeface.

Surveys: At most one short survey (up to 5 questions) is live at a time. It pops up once for you on the dashboard (once per person: answering it, or tapping Later, on one of your linked devices counts for all of them; on a device that isn't linked, the survey offers Link this device); tap Later and it waits at the top of your Inbox (on every hub and the dashboard, with a dot on the Inbox button) until you answer it. Where a question offers Other, picking it opens a box to type your own answer. Answering a survey earns +1,000 XP and +1,000 Shiny Gold Crowns, once for each survey ("Later" doesn't count until you answer it). A survey opens in the same window as the exam check-in, with Timmy peeking over the top and the reward on it, and answering it gets the same celebration and Collect. A survey you said "Later" to may pop up once more; it always waits in your Inbox too.

A top bar that fits your screen: On a narrow phone or at the largest text the dashboard's bar drops, in order, the studying-now count, the words "Study Hubs" and the rank badge. Nothing runs off the screen.
A little something on each hub: Each hub's drawn scene has something to say.

sections.title: In every hub
items: What every hub has, whatever its subject. Most of it is on the hub's bar or under More, where Talk to us holds the Inbox, Suggest, Report, the idea board, the tour, this page and the way back to the dashboard.

Hub tour: Every hub has its own guided tour with a spotlight on the real buttons. No pop-up on arrival any more: a one-line tip shows the first time you open each part of a hub. Take the tour under More (Talk to us).

Search: Searches the full text of the hub (notes paragraphs, review rows, exam hints, cram lines and questions) and jumps to the exact spot. Magic words typed here also work (that's how phones do the easter eggs). The magnifier on the hub's bar.

Daily drill: A set of questions a day per hub, fixed for the day: spaced-review questions that are due, questions you missed last time, then high-yield ones the class finds hard, spread across lectures. Each card says why it was picked. Pick the length before you start: 10, 20 or 30 questions (it remembers your choice). Finish for a results screen (the check draws itself, your score counts up, each question ticks in with a check or an X, and the drill streak rolls up when that set started today's streak), buttons for 10, 20 or 30 more, and a drill streak. Daily drill on a hub's Home, under Questions (the Sets row), the Daily drill button on the dashboard, or …/hubs/<hub>/#questions/drill.

Rewards on every answer: XP counts up on the rank pill in the bar, the goal ring fills, the day-streak flame grows with the streak, and Timmy cheers or flinches. When you leave the questions with 5 or more answered, a session recap card says how it went and offers the misses. It never interrupts practice.

Daily goal: A ring in the bar fills toward your goal: 10 to 50 questions a day (20 to start; change it in Settings). The streak still counts any day you answer a question; missing the goal doesn't break it. On Home, the goal is a ring of 20 teeth that fill in as you answer.

Answer feedback: Answer a question and a wash of green sweeps across the right choice with a soft glow and a check mark that draws itself. A wrong pick shakes and gets an X, then the right answer lights up. Select-all and ordering questions mark each option in turn, matching pairs light up as they lock in, and the explanation slides open. Works wherever you answer questions: the question bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill.

Streak flame: Get 3 right in a row and a flame appears in the bottom-right corner counting your run, with a ring that fills toward 100 (the tactical nuke). It grows and changes color as you go: orange at 5, red-hot at 10, blue at 25, violet at 50 and gold at 100. Miss one and it fizzles out in a puff of smoke. It counts the run on the page you're on, like the nuke. Off with Settings → Extras → Streak flame, or with Focus mode. (The flame on the hub's bar is a different one: it counts the days in a row you've studied.) It steps aside on the Mock Exam tab.

Smaller touches: Progress bars fill from where they were instead of jumping. Switching modes, tabs and lectures fades the new page in. If your device is set to reduce motion, the hubs keep the check and X marks and the results cards and skip the rest.
Spaced review: Every question you get right comes back after 1, then 2, 4 and 7 days, never later than the day before the exam. Misses come back sooner. It feeds the drill and Weak Spots.
Studying now: The green dot in the bar counts everyone on this hub right now, you included, and Home says it under the countdown. It's a live total: nothing about who.

Focus mode: One switch at the top of Settings turns Timmy and every extra off, for just the notes and the questions. Turning it off brings back what you had, and turning any one extra back on ends it. It uses the extras' own switches, so the dashboard and every hub follow it.

Class accuracy on every question: After you answer, the explanation shows what % of the class got it right. Explanations name the most popular wrong answer when it's a common trap. How the class answered : once you answer a multiple-choice or select-all question, every choice shows the % of the class that picked it, with a light bar behind it, and the most common pick is in bold. A wrong answer with a big share is the trap most people fall for. Your own answer is counted in, and the line under the explanation says how many answers it's based on. In the Question Bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill in every hub, and on your mock exam's results (never while you're taking it). It shows once at least one other person has answered that question. Every answer counts, so someone who answers a question three times counts three times. When a question's choices or its answer are edited, its percentages start again from the new choices' first answers, so an old number never sits beside a choice that changed . A reworded question (a different wording on a later try) counts with its original.

Why each choice: Every multiple-choice and select-all question explains each answer choice, not just the right one. After you answer, tap the folded "Why each choice" bar under the explanation to see why the right answer is right and what is wrong with each of the others, with your pick marked. It starts folded so it doesn't fill the screen. It shows in the Question Bank, the Daily Drill and when you review a mock exam. Every new question gets one too.

Find this in the notes: Miss a question and a Find this in the notes button appears under the explanation. Tap it to read the notes paragraph that matches the question, right there in the card, with its key words marked; Open this in the notes takes you to that spot in the lecture and highlights it. It works in the Question Bank, Weak Spots and the Daily drill (opening the notes closes the drill; it picks up where you left off), not in the mock exam or the arcade. When no paragraph matches well enough, the button doesn't show.

Good question?: Under every explanation, once you answer, a thumbs up or down for the question itself. A thumbs down asks what's wrong with it: the answer looks wrong, the wording is confusing, it isn't in the notes, the explanation didn't help, or it gives the answer away (for anything else, report it opens the Report form). Tap the same thumb again to take your vote back. Together with how the class does on each question (how many get it right the first time, who gets it right after missing it, how long it takes, whether people give up on it or skip the explanation), your votes put questions that may have a problem on a list that gets checked against the notes. Nothing changes a question on its own: a person reads it, and a fix goes out like any other. In the Question Bank, Weak Spots, the Daily drill and your mock exam's results (never while you're taking it), in every hub. One vote per question; it's remembered on this device.
Report an issue: A Report button on every question and under each lecture's notes, plus one under More. When it's fixed you get a reply in your Inbox saying what changed.

Suggest something: Send an idea for the hubs. Replies come back the same way. It's still private, to Sam. Tick Also post this on the idea board to put it on the board too, under your leaderboard name.

Listen: On Lecture Notes: pre-recorded narration of every lecture, at all three reading levels, with seek, ±15 s, speed, resume where you left off, and lock-screen controls. Controls that follow you : scroll away from the Listen button while it's reading and a small player bar stays at the bottom of the screen with play/pause, a progress bar you can drag, the time and a stop button. Tap the lecture's name on it to jump back up. A classmate's idea. Archived hubs : when a hub is archived after its exam, its recorded narration comes off the site (GitHub limits how big the site can be). Listen still works there, in your device's own voice. Follow along : while Listen plays a lecture's narration, the word being read is highlighted in the notes, with its sentence shaded more softly, and the page scrolls to keep it in view. Scroll away and it stops following until you come back (or move the narration: then it jumps there). The Follow along button beside Listen turns it off or back on, on this device. A classmate's idea, from the survey. Tap a word to jump there : while Listen plays a lecture's narration (or is paused), tap or click any word in the notes and the narration moves to that word and plays from it. On a phone too. Tapping a link, a diagram or one of your highlights does what it always did, and so does selecting text to highlight it. In a browser too old for it, Listen plays as before, without the highlight.

Highlighter: Select any text in the Lecture Notes and tap Highlight to mark it, or pick a color first: yellow, green, blue, pink or orange . Your last color is remembered, and tapping a highlight lets you change its color. Your highlights stay put when you come back, at that reading level, and Listen still works over them. Tap a highlight to recolor or remove it, or to clear every highlight in those notes. A classmate's idea. On a phone, the Highlight button now answers a tap (it only worked with a mouse before), and in the new hubs your colors show again (every highlight had come out gold). Highlights are saved on this device only, so they don't follow you to another phone or laptop. If a lecture's notes get rewritten, its old highlights are cleared rather than landing on the wrong words.

Timmy Time: A podcast episode for the night before the exam, hosted by Timmy Tooth (deep voice, small tooth). He walks through every lecture on the exam in the order the questions are weighted, quotes what the professors said would be tested and what to skip, and finishes with a lightning round where you answer out loud before he does. Music, chapters you can jump between, speeds from 1× to 2×, ±15/30 s, resume where you left off, and lock-screen controls. It keeps playing when you switch tabs or modes, with a small player pinned to the bottom of the screen. Listening counts as study time. Likes and comments : under every episode you can like or dislike it, read what the class thought and add your own comment (it posts under your leaderboard name, up to 280 characters). The thread starts folded to its first comment: tap Show more comments for the rest. Delete your own any time; report anyone else's, and a comment with three reports is hidden until it's checked. A few comments come from Timmy's world (his neighbor number thirty-one, for one): they're the ones with a tag and a dashed border. It's in the quick links on the hub's Home, under More → Timmy Time, and under the hub on the dashboard. Episodes so far: MSK Exam 4 (42 min), the Occlusion midterm (45 min, with Dr. Givan's fence post walked through step by step), Heme & Endo Exam 1 (53 min, all ten lectures gland by gland, with the 10/28 review's answers), PCD Implants Exam 1 (48 min, all nine lectures and every item on the course's hint list), Heme & Endo Exam 2 (52 min, L11-L16 with the lab patterns the class keeps flipping, the two picture questions, and a quick Exam 1 refresher), the Perio final (52 min, all nine sessions weighted like the final toward Sessions 5-9, what Dr. Abou-Arraj's review said to know and to skip, Dr. Geurs' regeneration class in his own words, and Dr. Kaur's three implant states, health, mucositis and peri-implantitis), the Occlusion final (48 min, L6-L10: the articulator and its records, splints and bruxism, the three denture schemes side by side, Dr. Lawson's cervical lesions and Dr. Abou-Arraj's occlusal trauma, with both mobility scales) and Heme & Endo Exam 3 (52 min, Dr. Taylor's Lecture A and L17-L22, each lecture opening on Dr. Herr's study guide list, with the leukemias on their two axes and the five translocations). A hub carries one episode at a time: the Occlusion final's took the midterm's place. The file is big (30 to 40 MB), so it only downloads when you press play. An episode comes off the site with its hub's narration when the hub is archived after the exam.

Moving around the notes: On a laptop the lecture list down the side scrolls on its own, so the last lectures are always one scroll away instead of at the bottom of the notes. At the end of every lecture's notes, Previous and Next take you straight to the lecture before or after it, back at the top. Diagrams you can play with now fit on the screen with their buttons: the drawing stays pinned at the top while its options and explanation scroll up under it, so you can change a setting and watch the drawing at the same time. Report a problem with these notes : a button under each lecture's notes for a typo, a mistake or something confusing in that lecture. It goes to the same place as a question report, and you get a reply in your Inbox when it's fixed. In every hub.

Three ways to read: As taught (the professor's version), Plain English (the same facts in everyday words) and High yield: only what's most likely on the exam. High yield lists each predicted topic (the same list as Exam hints' "Most likely questions"), strongest evidence first, with the part of the notes that teaches it and the professor's own "know this", then what else was flagged in class and what you can skip. Its button at the end opens that lecture's High likelihood questions. Listen reads all three, with Follow along.

Study guide: When a professor hands out a study guide, it gets its own page at the top of the Notes' lecture list. Every item on the guide is a heading, with what the professor said in class about it (quoted from the hub's Exam Hints), a short Know this list, a side-by-side table where one helps, and the mix-ups to watch for. Each lecture then has what else was stressed in class, what was said not to be needed, and the guide's key terms, defined in a line. Each lecture's part ends with buttons to its notes and to its High likelihood questions. That button opens just the lecture's study guide questions, and a Practice all study guide questions button under the lecture buttons opens every one (the bank's On the study guide filter). Buttons at the top jump to a lecture, Listen plays it (in the notes' narrator's voice when it has been recorded, with Follow along: tap a word to jump there), highlighting works as in the notes, and search finds it. First made for Heme & Endo Exam 3, for Dr. Herr's Exam 3 study guide.
Mind maps: "Show mind map" under each lecture draws its outline as a branching tree.

Settings: Focus mode, Theme, Text size (Small to XX-Large), your daily goal, your display name, and the extras, each with its own switch: Timmy Tooth (On / Dashboard only / Off; off, an Ask button takes his place), Hidden secrets (holidays, magic words and the other easter eggs), Plaque bosses, Tooth Fairy, Golden Probe, Tactical nukes (On / Mine only, which hides classmates' strikes / Off), Rank-up and trophy cards, Streak cheers (confetti and a toast every 5 in a row), Streak flame, and Answer animations (off keeps the check and X marks, and stops the pop-ups' and pages' entrances). The same switches in every hub's Settings and the dashboard's. The font choice, background sound and accent metals are gone. The gear on the hub's bar, or More → Settings.
Install as an app: "Add to Home Screen" gives a Gold-handpiece app icon and opens full screen. Pages load from cache when the connection is bad.

What the hubs record: There's no sign-in and no email. Your browser gets a random id, kept on this device, that ties your progress, rank and trophies together (Link my devices joins two browsers). Under that id the hubs save: time in each part of a hub (only while the tab is in view and you've used it in the last 15 minutes, or while a lecture's narration or Timmy Time is playing, even with the screen off), which buttons and tabs you tap, your answers (right or wrong, which choice, whether it was your first try, which version of the question you saw, and how long you spent on the question and on its explanation; a question you read for a few seconds and leave unanswered is noted too), which features you use (Listen, Timmy Time, diagrams, the drill) and which settings you have on, and whatever you send (reports, suggestions, check-ins, surveys, comments, a thumbs up or down on a question). Words typed into Search are saved with no id at all. While you have a hub open, the dashboard's "studying now" count includes you, along with the outfit your Timmy has on, with no name or id; none of that is saved, and it's gone when you close the tab. Nothing else you type is recorded, no IP address, location or device details are saved with your data, and there are no ad or analytics trackers from other companies. It's used to make the hubs better for the whole class: what gets used, which questions trip people up, what to fix before the next exam. Only Sam sees study data per person. Classmates see only what the hubs are built to show: leaderboards, trophies and comments under your leaderboard name (a generated dentistry name unless you pick one), and class-wide numbers such as the share of the class who got a question right. Nothing is used to grade or judge anyone. Clearing this site's data in your browser starts a new id, and your progress on that device goes with it. How long it's kept : time in each part of a hub is saved in 25-second steps for 3 days , then only as hourly totals. Which buttons and tabs you tapped is kept for 90 days, and which features you used for 180 days; after that only class-wide daily totals remain, with no id. A report or suggestion loses your id 120 days after Sam replies (what it said and the reply stay), a survey answer 90 days after the survey closes, and an exam check-in after a year. Your answers, XP, rank and trophies are kept, because your progress is built from them. The cleanup runs by itself every night. With the redesign: your chats with Ask Timmy are saved, every message with your browser's id, to help improve the hub (Sam reads them on the admin page to fix gaps in the notes and wrong answers). They're answered by Claude, Anthropic's AI: your question, the hub's notes and what's on your screen go to Anthropic's API to write the answer, and nowhere else. When the notes don't cover something and Timmy looks it up, the search words he writes for it go from Anthropic to its web search provider; nothing about you goes with them. Only Sam and your own browser can read your chats; classmates never see them. An idea you post on the idea board shows to the class under your leaderboard name, and so does a check-in's "What could the hub have done better?" unless you untick the box. Your votes and reports on ideas are kept so each person counts once; nobody else sees who voted or reported. How you rated each flashcard and where you are in Learn are kept, so your schedule and progress follow you to your other devices. What you bought in Timmy's shop and what's out at his place are kept, so they stay yours on every device. Counted, with nothing about who or which: opening Timmy's place and changing something there (which spot, never which piece); opening the shop, a purchase (its kind: an outfit, a snack, a boost, never which piece) and a rare costume turning up; opening your collections and a collection's bonus paid by the shop (never which collection); a visit to someone's place (that one happened, never whose); a bowling clip playing (which clip, never who saw it). The clips you've seen and your run of right answers are kept on your device only. When the database is busy and an answer doesn't save, it waits on your device and goes once it can: later on the same page, or the next time you open that hub, within 3 days. It counts and pays once, however many times it's sent. A mock exam's or an arcade game's answers wait the same way, and its score and bonus are worked out once they've all arrived. The outfit your Timmy has on goes with the studying-now count, with no name or id, and isn't saved.

sections.title: Inside a hub
items: Each hub has four parts on its bar: Home, Notes, Questions and More. On a laptop the bar is at the top; on a phone it's at the bottom, with a Settings button beside the four. Your answers, pins, highlights and progress in each hub carried over from the old pages.
Back to the dashboard: Always on the screen in a hub: All hubs at the start of the bar on a laptop, Hubs at the start of the top strip on a phone. (More → All hubs is still there.)

Pages and pop-ups move: A hub's pages slide in from the side their tab is on, the tab you tapped pops, a hub's panel on the dashboard slides in the same way, and every pop-up window (the shop, Timmy's place, the trophy case, the Inbox, a check-in, a survey) rises into place. Off with your device's reduced-motion setting or Settings → Answer animations. The drawn pictures move when you get to them: the leaderboard's stage, the classroom, the picture of Timmy's place, the road, the idea board's Timmy and the shop's frames come alive for a few seconds when they come on screen, when you stop scrolling and under a mouse, then rest. They hold still while you scroll, so the page stays smooth.

Home: Every hub opens on its own Home: the hub's masthead, the exam card (a live countdown and the announced facts), quick links on the first phone screen (practice questions, Daily drill, the notes you were on, the mock, and Timmy Time when the hub has an episode), Where to next (at most three: yesterday's misses in exam week, your weakest lecture, a lecture not started), Today (the goal as a ring of 20 teeth, your streak, XP today, right today, your Shiny Gold Crowns, which open Timmy's shop, and Timmy's HP), progress by lecture with Notes and Questions buttons, and the course timeline. Under the countdown: how many are studying this hub right now. A hub with two exams (Review of Systems' two mock boards) counts down to the first, then to the second once the first is over.

Notes: The lecture list (lectures on the exam first, the others for review, each with a progress bar and how many questions you've tried; in a hub of several courses, each course's parts under its name, labeled by course: HN-1, F2-3), with a professor's study guide at the top when there is one, three reading levels (As taught, Plain English, High yield), Listen with Follow along, the drawn diagrams beside their paragraph, each lecture's charts under its notes, and Check yourself: three questions at the end of each lecture's notes. Cover the answers: every chart (under a lecture's notes and on More → Side by side) can hide everything but each row's first column, so it works as a self-test: tap Show on a cell to check that one, or Show all. Topics fold: tap a topic's heading (or the arrow beside it) to fold it away and again to open it, and Collapse all in the toolbar turns a lecture into a list of its topics to open one at a time (Expand all brings them back). It works in all three reading levels and on a professor's study guide (each item folds, under its lecture), and this device remembers what you folded. A search result, Open this in the notes or Listen opens a folded topic when it gets there. At the end, Previous lecture / Next lecture, and Report a mistake in these notes (also in the notes toolbar), which opens the report form with the lecture attached.

Questions: The Question Bank, its filter panel (with the High likelihood toggle) and four sets: Daily drill, Yesterday's misses, Weak spots and Mock exam. Answer choices are plain rows with a check or a cross after you answer; Pin and Report are on every card. After an answer, one row: Try it again, Find this in the notes (on a miss), Ask Timmy and Good question?. Pick how many questions come at a time, and every card is numbered. At a time, beside Order in the filters, is 50, 100 (where it starts), 200 or All. A longer list is split into sets of that size: with 100, the cards say Question 12 of 100, and above the list Questions 101–200 of 845 shows which set you're on, with Previous, Next and a list to jump to any of them. At the end of a set, Next 100 questions takes you to the next one. When your filters leave fewer than that (one lecture, say), there's one set and the cards count what's there: Question 12 of 84; with All, it's one long list (Question 12 of 845). Changing the size keeps your place: on 101–200, picking 50 takes you to 101–150. The Daily drill counts the ones you've already done today (your first one left might be Question 6 of 20), and the mock numbers its questions too. A missed question that comes back a few cards later isn't counted again. The bank remembers your size, and which set you were on while your filters stay the same, so you can take a break at Question 40 and come back to the same set. Not answered yet and Missed last time always start at their first set, since what you've answered drops out of them.

Study as: Questions, Learn or Flashcards: At the top of Questions. The panel picks which questions; this picks how. Learn and Flashcards show a card with how far along you are and a Start button, then take the whole screen, one card at a time, like Quizlet: a Close button (or Escape) puts you back in the bank, and your progress is kept. Learn asks the questions you picked in rounds of 7 until you've got each right twice (the second time, when the question allows it, you think of the answer before the choices show; a miss comes back at the end of the round). The choices are big tiles (keys 1 to 6 pick one on a laptop), Don't know? shows the answer without a guess, and after a right answer it moves on by itself unless you touch the card to read why (the Auto-next switch turns that off). A bar along the top shows how far along you are, and each round ends with what you got. Flashcards show the question on a card; you flip it (Flip the card, a tap on the card or the space bar) and say how well you knew it: Again, Hard, Good or Easy, keys 1 to 4, the left and right arrows for Again and Good, or on a phone a swipe left for Again and right for Good. It comes back when you're about to forget it, never later than the day before the exam. When you're caught up you see how the session went, rating by rating. Home tells you when cards are due. Learn's answers count like any answer. A flashcard counts toward your daily goal and streak (not as an answer: no class stats, no "Last time") and earns 2 XP when it's due or new, for its first three ratings a day; Study ahead earns none. Drill, Yesterday's misses and Weak spots work in all three; the mock exam is always questions.

Question types: Multiple choice, select-all with partial credit, matching, ordering, two-statement, EXCEPT / NOT, Patient Box cases and picture questions, each in the exam's own format. Which statement is true, or false? : four full statements, and you pick the one true statement (or, in the inverse, the one false statement among three true ones). Each false statement changes one detail you were taught, never a trick of wording, and every choice explains itself once you answer. Find them under the Question Bank's More filters → question type (every new lecture of a course exam gets them; Review of Systems is all board-style multiple choice). Patient cases drawn from their numbers : in a hub with dental Patient Box cases (PCD Implants and Perio had them; neither page is up now), the cases come with a periodontal chart, a periapical radiograph and a drawn view of the gums, all produced from the same case numbers (probing depths, recession, bleeding, mobility, furcations, bone levels, restorations, implants), the way the Perio midterm check-ins asked. Every tooth is drawn from its real anatomy (the sizes and shapes in Wheeler's Dental Anatomy: the right cusps, the right number of roots, the long canine root, the root trunk above a molar's furcation), and every number in a case is checked to be realistic and to agree with the others before it ships. The chart is drawn like a probing chart (blue line for the gingival margin, red line for the pocket base, red dots for bleeding, furcation triangles), with the numbers in a table under it. Everything you need to answer is in the box before you answer, and a picture never shows the answer: a question that asks you to work out the attachment level hides the CAL row, one that asks the furcation class hides the furcation row. After you answer, "Why each choice" explains every option and In the notes buttons jump to the notes paragraph and Review table the case comes from. The drawings are illustrations made from the numbers, never patient photos or real radiographs. Numbered statements : in the Heme & Endo hubs (and every hub from now on, at least two per lecture), "Which statements are true? 1... 2... 3... 4..." questions answered with a combination ("1, 2 and 4", "2 and 3 only"). The combinations always come in the same order, the Question Bank's format filter has them too, and after you answer, "Why each choice" says which statement each wrong combination got wrong. Heme & Endo also has two-statement and true-or-false questions for every lecture (the Question Bank's type filter has "True or false" and "Numbered statements").

Question Bank filters: The Question Bank's filters sit in one labeled panel above the questions. Lectures opens a list with a tick box per lecture, so you can practice any mix; tap Only on a row for just that one. In a hub of several courses (Review of Systems), the list puts each course's parts under its name, and the course's own Only picks all of its parts at once. Show picks All, Not answered yet, Missed last time or Pinned, and each chip says how many questions you'd get. Only, under it, is the High likelihood tick box, which works on top of whichever Show chip you picked: tick it with Missed last time for the likely-exam questions you got wrong, with Not answered yet for the ones you haven't tried, with Pinned for the ones you saved, or with All for every one of them. Tap it again to turn it off. A hub with a professor's study guide adds a second tick box there, On the study guide: only the questions on the guide: of the High likelihood questions that come from it, one or two on each point it names, without the repeats, with the same Show chips on top. High likelihood still has every one. One tick box is on at a time. Order is In order (lecture by lecture) or Random (tap it again to reshuffle). More filters adds the question type (true or false, two statements, Patient Box, matching and the rest) and where a question comes from. Under the panel, a line says how many questions are showing and lists every filter that's on: tap one to take it off, or Clear all. If nothing matches, it says which filter is in the way and gives you a button back to the whole bank. In every hub built since Heme & Endo Exam 3. The bank opens with the lectures, filters and order you used last time (the search box starts empty), and the line under the panel shows them, so you always know what's hidden. A Sets row under Show: Daily drill, Yesterday's misses, Weak spots and Mock exam. A set replaces the list until you close it; your filters stay as they were. On a laptop a Today column (the goal ring, streak, XP, this session) sits beside the questions.

High Likelihood Exam Questions: Each hub predicts the topics most likely to be on its exam, lecture by lecture, from what the professors flagged in the recordings, in-class reviews and focus lists, the class exam-review guide and what earlier check-ins said the exam asked. The questions on those topics carry a High Likelihood Exam Question tag in the Question Bank and the Daily drill (never in the mock exam, which stays exam-like). Each topic shows where it came from. Tap the tag to see why. On a question card (and a flashcard), the High likelihood tag opens a short note: the predicted topic the question belongs to, where it ranks among its lecture's topics (strongest evidence first), and what the prediction rests on, such as a hint from the professor, the final's review, the class's review guide, the study guide or the slides, with a link to every predicted topic in Exam hints. Review of Systems says High yield instead. Its topics and quotes come from the courses it reviews, from what each course stressed for its own exams, so they mark high-yield content but don't predict the mocks: the tag, the bank's toggle and High yield say High yield, and Exam hints is High-yield points. Open Exam Hints → Most likely questions for the list, with a Practice these button per lecture. In the Question Bank, tick High likelihood (the Only line, under Show) to practice only those questions , together with Not answered yet, Missed last time or Pinned if you like; untick it for the whole bank. In every live hub and every hub built from now on.

Pinned questions: Every question card has a Pin button next to Report. Pin the ones you want to come back to, and the Question Bank's Pinned chip (under Show) shows only those, still with your lecture picks and order. Tap Pinned again on a card to unpin it. In every hub built since Heme & Endo Exam 3. Pins follow you to your other devices once they're linked (Settings → Link my devices); an unpin on one device unpins it everywhere.

Statements come back in a new order: When a numbered-statement question ("Which statements are true? 1... 2... 3... 4...") or a two-statement question comes back, its statements are shuffled and renumbered, and every choice follows them: a choice still means the same statements, under their new numbers. The choices stay in their usual order, so the right one moves too, and "the answer was 1, 2 and 4" won't carry over from last time: you have to judge each statement again. The card's top line says new order, and "Why each choice" and the explanation use the numbers on your screen. It's the same question with the same answer, and it counts exactly as before. In every hub, from a question's second try on (the Question Bank, the Daily drill, Yesterday's misses, Weak spots, a missed question that comes back, Learn and Flashcards); your first try shows the original order, and the mock keeps it too. Ask Timmy talks about the statements by the numbers you saw, and a report says which order you were shown.

Missed it? Try it again: In every hub's Question Bank, a question you miss comes back as a fresh card five questions further down the list, marked Try it again ( in the new hubs: a tinted card with a dashed edge and a Second try band across the top), so you get a second rep while it is still fresh instead of only at the end (or through the "Missed last time" filter). Miss it again and it comes back again, as the Third try. A patient's questions stay together, so it never lands in the middle of a case. A classmate's idea.

Undo on ordering questions: Tapped a step by mistake? Undo last step takes back your latest tap and Start over clears them all. Both show up once you've tapped a step and go away when the question is graded.

Diagrams: Drawn diagrams sit right inside the Lecture Notes, next to the paragraph they explain (and in Review). Each one has a folded Show the key under it (what each arrow, border or part is), so you can test yourself first, and picture questions ask you to read one: the key stays hidden until you answer, then the explanation shows the diagram with its key open.
Submit at the bottom: Mock exams now have a second Submit exam button (with the answered count) after the last question, so you don't have to scroll back to the top to hand it in.

Mock exam results: Submit a mock exam and a results card opens: your score counts up while a ring fills (gold at 90%+, green at 75%+), a one-line verdict, your best mock in that hub on this device ("New personal best, up from 72%"), and a bar per lecture so you can see where the misses were. 90% or better gets a celebration. "See what I missed" jumps straight to the questions you got wrong; "Review answers" shows them all.

More: A tile per part, each on its own color with a line of what's in it: Timmy Time (the big one, Timmy in headphones), Exam hints, Cram sheet, Side by side (the charts that compare across lectures; it was Review), Arcade, Timmy's place, Timmy's shop, Stats and trophies and Settings. Then Talk to us: Inbox, Suggest something, Report a problem, the Idea board, Take the tour, About and All hubs.

Arcade: Under More, in a hub that has one (Review of Systems doesn't). The lobby shows every game, each on its own color with its own drawing, the hub's pick first. Six games per hub (next part), with the option to play only the questions you missed. Games built on the question bank count toward your stats, XP and Timmy's health.

sections.title: Arcade games
items: Every game has a class-wide high-score board. In a hub with an arcade it is under More, and its lobby shows every game on its own color with its own drawing. Every hub's arcade has the same six games and rules, each with its own names and look (Review of Systems has no arcade). The action games almost nobody played (snake, flappy, whack-a-mole and the rest) are gone, and three new quiz games came out of your survey answers. In every game built on the question bank, Questions from picks a lecture or Questions I missed, which replays only the ones you got wrong last time.
Game · What it is

Showdown · A Jeopardy-style board: one column per lecture, $100 (the question the class gets right most) to $500 (the toughest). Right adds the value, wrong takes it away. Two tiles hide a wager round, and a final question lets you bet it all.

Lab Escape · A point-and-click escape room. The door locked behind you; tap things in the room and answer the questions that lock them to find the four digits of the door code. Six minutes, and every wrong answer costs 20 seconds. One digit needs an item you find in the room.

Fill in the blank · Fill in the blank, Anki cloze style: a sentence straight from the lecture notes with a key term taken out. Type it before the clock runs down (a typo of a letter or two still counts). Three lives.
Quiz show · 12 rungs to $125,000, three lifelines (50:50, Ask the class, Swap). Something on screen turns gold as you climb.
Crossword · A fresh mini crossword every game, from the course terms.
Sort · Fling falling cards into the right bin (each lecture's look-alikes).

sections.title: Ranks, mastery and recognition
items: XP: 10 XP the first time you get a question right, 2 for any other right answer, 1 for a miss, and a flat 2 for a card you grade yourself, plus 20 for every day you study. There is no daily cap any more. Every right answer pays, however quickly you answer and however many times you get that question right in a day (tapping the same answer twice still counts once). A miss pays for a question's first three each day, and misses less than 2 seconds apart (or more than 30 in a minute) still count but earn nothing. Counted across every hub.

More ways to earn XP: +30 at your 20th answer of the day; +50 for a mock exam with 10 or more answers (once a hub a day); +50 for finishing an arcade game (each game once a day, after 20 seconds of play); 10 for each minute of a Timmy Time episode you hear for the first time (most of the minute, up to twice as fast) and +100 for finishing it; +100 when a report or suggestion you sent is fixed; +1,000 (and 1,000 Shiny Gold Crowns) for each survey you answer and your first check-in for each exam; and +100, +200, +300 and +500 for a hub's Bronze, Silver, Gold and Crown medals.

The reward card: When something pays a bonus (today's goal, 10, 25 or 50 right in a row, a streak of days, a medal, a lecture read to the end, a finished mock or arcade game, Timmy Time, a trophy, a Plaque Boss, the nuke; and on the dashboard, a visit to a classmate's Timmy, your leaderboard name and a trophy), a gold card pops up with what you did and the XP and Shiny Gold Crowns it paid, counting up, with a burst of confetti; then the stars and coins fly into your rank (on the dashboard, into your crowns). On a laptop it comes up at the bottom of the screen; on a phone it drops in at the top, clear of Timmy and the tab bar. Bonuses that arrive together share one card. Tap it to close it. With reduced motion or "Answer animations" off it simply fades in and out.

Double XP: Every new mastery medal starts 24 hours of double XP on answers, the day's bonuses, mocks and games (never more than 2x; a new medal starts the 24 hours again). A gold "2x" chip on your rank shows the time left, and the XP that flies up from an answer says "2x". Timmy's shop sells one-hour and three-hour boosts too. Double XP you bought is never wasted under a medal's: a boost bought during a medal's 24 hours starts when they end, and one still running when you win a medal keeps the rest of its time for after the medal's 24 hours.

Three journeys: The handpiece ladder is the first of three. Handpiece: Stone (start), Antique (300 XP), Bronze (1,500), Silver (5,000), Gold (12,000), Diamond (25,000), Dark Matter (50,000). At 125,000 XP the ModuPro begins (the sim-lab typodont), and at 250,000 the Loupes, each with the same seven ranks, evenly spaced, each rank with levels I, II and III. Nothing is lost on the way: your XP, trophies and Timmy's place come with you. From the ModuPro on your rank reads "ModuPro Gold II". The road on the dashboard lays all three out, rank by rank, and More → Stats and trophies shows the road ahead too.

Rank-up celebrations: A new rank plays a full-screen cutscene (your old medallion charges up, a flash, the new one), and a new level flips in like a coin, each with the journey's own object. Two more full-screen scenes: reaching Dark Matter is the biggest moment on the ladder: everything is pulled into your Diamond medallion until it collapses into a single point, then it explodes into the Dark Matter medallion with shock waves and the journey's own sky (once per journey, ever, on whichever device gets there first). It pays 5,000 Shiny Gold Crowns, counted up on the screen with a shower of coins, and on the Handpiece it shows the two Legendary pieces it unlocks for Timmy's place. Skip there jumps to the reward. And finishing a journey hands you the next object: for the ModuPro, a typodont (its 32 teeth drawn to Wheeler's crown shapes) comes in with its jaws wide open around your Dark Matter Handpiece and pulls it into its mouth with a rush of dust and stars, then bites down, chews it to pieces with shards flying out of the corners, swallows, and becomes your ModuPro medallion as the sim lab's light comes on: "The ModuPro is yours." For the Loupes, a pair of loupes comes down over your Dark Matter ModuPro and its headlight clicks on; the beam grows into a sunbeam that heats the ModuPro white-hot until it cracks and burns away into embers, and the loupes come down through the light into its place. Reaching a new journey pays too: 20,000 Shiny Gold Crowns for the ModuPro and 30,000 for the Loupes, counted up on the screen with a shower of coins, with the trophy for the journey you finished. All of them can be skipped, wait until a mock exam is over, are one still card with reduced motion, and are off with Settings → Extras → Rank-up and trophy cards.
Hub mastery: The share of a hub's question bank you got right on your latest try: Bronze 50%, Silver 75%, Gold 90%, Crown 100%.

Mastery medals: Each hub you master earns a medal of its own: the metal is the tier (Bronze, Silver, Gold, or Gold with a crown on top for Crown), and the emblem and ribbons belong to the hub (a probe for Perio, meeting cusps for Occlusion, a bone for MSK 3, a flexed arm for MSK 4, a crown on a prep for PCD). On every leaderboard (rank, streak, correct-in-a-row, both arcades and Tooth Fairy collectors) one medal sits next to your name: the medal for the hub you're in, or your best one on the dashboard, then "+N" for the rest. Tap it to see all of someone's medals. Your rank card shows each one with its hub's name. A new medal gets its own card (below).

Trophy case: 27 trophies, in More → Stats and trophies in a hub, or from the Trophy case button on your card on the dashboard. Your rank sits on top with the road ahead. Then a showcase stand with one trophy at a time (it opens on your rarest; tap any trophy to put it there) and a cabinet with three shelves: Won by studying (8), The journeys (3: Handpiece, ModuPro and Loupes finished) and Secrets (16). A trophy you've won is lit on its brass plate with the share of the class that has it; one you haven't is dimmed, with what earns it; a secret you haven't found is only its shape and its clue, with how many have found it. Under those, a shelf for each hub with its own eight: the four mastery medals (Bronze, Silver, Gold and the Crown, in that hub's emblem), Seen It All, Mock Ace, Perfect Mock and a secret. If you won Full Arch before it was retired, it stays in your case on a "Retired" shelf. The leaderboards are behind the Leaderboards button.

Your stats: Under the case: your numbers on a scoreboard (answered, right, best run, days you met your goal), a card for each lecture with how you're doing (your strongest and the one that needs work marked), and your achievements.

Trophy and medal cards: A new trophy or medal pops up framed in its metal, drawn, with the share of the class that has it and what's next ("12 of 27 in your case", "Gold at 90% right"). A new rank names the pieces it brings to Timmy's place. They take turns, wait until a mock exam is submitted, are one still card with reduced motion, and are off with Settings → Extras → Rank-up and trophy cards.

Link my devices: Make a 6-character code on one device and enter it on another within 10 minutes (or send yourself the link and open it there); both then count as you (XP, streaks, trophies). Your question progress follows you too: questions you tried on your phone show up as tried (and right or missed) on your laptop the next time you open that hub, and the Daily Drill brings back misses from both. Answers you gave before linking come along. A hub also catches up when you come back to it after a few minutes away. If you use the hubs from your phone's home screen, type the code there rather than opening the link: a link can open in the browser instead, which counts as a separate device. It sits next to your name wherever you can change it: Settings (on the dashboard and in a hub's More), the dashboard's You card, the window that opens when you tap your name, and "Posting as" on the idea board and under Timmy Time.

"Is this your other device?": If you save a name that another device already uses, you keep the name and a card asks whether that device is yours too. Tap "Yes, link them" and it shows a code and a link, good for 10 minutes: right then, type the code on your other device (Settings, Link my devices next to your name; it links as soon as the sixth character is in), or send yourself the link and open it there ("Link this device?", one tap). Already have a code up on your other device? Type it on the card's first screen. Or tap "No, that's someone else" and it won't ask about that name again. A device whose name is shared is also asked once a day until you answer ("Not now" waits 3 days), and only about a device someone has used in the last 3 weeks.

sections.title: Timmy Tooth
items: Your cartoon tooth buddy. Everyone has one. Settings → Timmy Tooth: On, Dashboard only, or Off. Nobody else can see his health.

Everyone has Timmy: Nobody has to adopt him any more: he's there from your first visit, on the dashboard's You card and in the bottom-left corner of every hub, and he says hello. A Timmy you meet from the redesign on starts at full health, 100 HP; one you already had keeps his health and his history. Your other linked devices count his health from the day you first met him.
Where he lives: On the dashboard's You card, at his place (Timmy's place, below), and in the bottom-left corner of every hub with a health bar. He hides during mock exams.

Health: 0 to 100 HP, worked out from your answers in every hub. Each right answer heals 0.8 HP (up to 30 a day), each day in a row adds a streak bonus (up to 10), and each skipped day costs 8, then 12, 16 and 20 HP the longer you're away. At 0 he can't die, but he heals at half speed until he's back to 50.

What goes wrong: Below 70 HP: plaque. Below 55: brown stains and red, puffy gums (gingivitis). Below 40: a cavity. Below 25: periodontitis (recession, calculus, loose). Below 12: a cracked cusp. At 0: a bandage. Each goes away as he heals, and he thanks you.

Talking to him: Tap him for one of 73 dental jokes (plus holiday and fall jokes in season), a true tooth fact, one of his own thoughts, or a word about the outfit he's wearing; every few taps he gives a status update or a secret tip. "Tell me a joke" on the dashboard's You card is always a joke. Tap 5 times fast and he complains it tickles. "Checkup" opens his chart: health, today's answers, streak, and every condition. He deals his lines from shuffled decks, so you hear a whole set before any line comes back.

Ask Timmy: Tap Timmy and pick Ask me (on the dashboard, Ask me on the You card) to ask about the notes. He answers from the hub's own notes, review tables, Exam Hints and cram sheet only (on the dashboard, from every live hub's), in a few short lines, with a From the notes link under each point that opens the notes at that very paragraph. When the notes don't cover something he says so and points to the closest lecture. And then he looks it up. When the notes don't cover a term or a fact (say, what an exostosis is), he searches a short list of trusted medical and dental sites (NIH and PubMed, MedlinePlus, the Merck Manual, the ADA, the AAP and other dental associations, Radiopaedia, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic, the CDC) and adds a few sentences in a box marked Not in your notes · looked up, with a link to each source. It's only for what the notes leave out: anything the notes cover, he answers from the notes. If those sites don't answer it, you get the closest lecture alone. Starter questions: "What should I study tonight?" (he reads your own progress in the hub: weakest lectures, questions missed, lectures not started; it's worked out on your device and sent only with that question; on the dashboard it includes your answers from your linked devices, so a new phone knows what you've done), "Explain this lecture simply" (while you're in its notes), "What's most likely on the exam?" and "How do I use this hub?" (on the dashboard, "When are my exams?" and "What can this site do?"). He won't answer a graded quiz, take-home or exam question, and gives no hints on a practice question before you've answered it. 40 questions a day; after that he naps until tomorrow. Paused during a mock exam. Thumbs up or down on each answer, Report on any answer that's wrong or odd (Sam sees the whole chat and replies in your Inbox), and past chats on this hub (the clock). Chats are saved to help improve the hub: see What the hubs record.

If he spots a problem or an idea: He writes it up for you: a report for Sam or an idea for the idea board, in a box you can edit. Nothing is sent until you tap Send (or Post); No thanks drops it. An idea goes up under your leaderboard name.
Ask Timmy on a question: After you answer a practice question, Ask Timmy under it opens the chat with that question attached ("Why is it ...?"). Not before you answer.

Timmy off?: When Timmy is turned off (Settings, Dashboard only on a hub, or Focus mode), an Ask button sits in his spot (a hub's bottom-left corner; the You card on the dashboard) and the same chat answers in a plain "Ask the hub" voice, with the same rules.
Secret tips: He tells you how to find every easter egg, one at a time. The "Secret tip" button on the dashboard's You card, every 4th tap, or sometimes as his hello in a hub.

Reactions: He greets you differently by time of day, day of the week and month, and notices what's going on: a skipped day or a long absence, your study streak, a big day of questions, a second visit, an exam within the week, his own place, and how long you've had him (one week, a month, 100 days and more). He cheers at 3, 5, 10 and more right in a row, winces at misses, encourages you after a bad run and celebrates the comeback, comments when you switch modes, reacts to every easter egg, naps if you go idle for 3 minutes, nudges you to take a break on long sessions, and gives pep talks the day before and the day of an exam.

Outfits: He wears what you put on him at his place (Customize → Timmy), from the shop or from your rank, and nothing when nothing is on: on the bar, on the dashboard, at his place, in the classroom and on the leaderboard's stage. Holiday looks are in the shop's seasonal sets. He no longer dresses himself for holidays.

Timmy's place: Timmy has a place of his own: a home, the scene around it and a yard with five spots. It is on the dashboard's You card and in every hub under More → Timmy's place. Tap the picture to step in: it opens like a small theater, the place on a gold-framed stage under a row of lights, with Timmy today beside it (how he is doing, his HP on a meter), your rank, your hub medals, and the buttons Customize, Shop and Collections (next to it, how many you've finished). Timmy at home: tap anything and he hops over to it; tap him and he waves, and again while he's waving for a flip. How he moves is his health: at 90 HP and up he bounces and wanders the most, lower down he slows, and when he needs treatment he stays on the doorstep and tells you what he needs. Studying is still what heals him. Your rank and your medals live there: a statue of your rank stands by the door, in your rank's metal, on one step for each level. Past the Handpiece the ModuPro joins it on the pedestal, and in the Loupes journey Timmy wears his loupes. Every hub you've earned a mastery medal in hangs its medal on the board by the house (up to twenty; tap the board to see them all, in each hub's colors). Customize: change the home, the scene, what stands in each yard spot, the home's upgrades and paint, and what Timmy wears, from what you own. Every change is saved as you make it and follows you to your other linked devices. The bowling lane is long: it takes the side yard and the front corner together. "Surprise me" picks a whole new look, every piece you own sits in its rarity's frame (the same card art as the shop's: plain for Common, vines for Uncommon, a gem for Rare, stars for Epic, gold rays for Legendary), the piece in use has a gold tick, a rank piece you haven't reached is gray with the rank that gives it, and Done takes you back to the visit. What you own: the cottage on the hill is every Timmy's first home. Halloween 2026's set is a gift to everyone, each full rank-up gives an outfit and a yard piece (earned, never sold; the ModuPro's and the Loupes' fourteen ranks now have theirs too: the ModuPro's are the sim lab's, from a half-carved stone molar and a brass articulator to a golden dental chair, a giant diamond bur and a nebula in a bell jar, and the Loupes' are things for seeing by, from a sundial and a brass telescope to a microscope, a lighthouse, a prism and a Dark Matter observatory, with outfits Timmy wears over his loupes), and everything else is bought in Timmy's shop with Shiny Gold Crowns. What you own is yours for good, on every device you link; spending never lowers your XP or your rank. Seasons: the yard follows the year (spring blossom, fall leaves, winter snow), and on Timmy's holidays the place puts out its holiday props. Timmy himself wears what you put on him. The study-streak flame has two more colors: blue from 10 days in a row and Dark Matter from 30.

Timmy's shop: Shiny Gold Crowns are the hubs' money, for Timmy's shop. You earn 5 for every 10 XP (it was 1, and the crowns from all the XP you've already earned went up with it; a boost's extra XP doesn't count), 100 for every hour you spend in a hub (the same time your stats count, all of it so far; at most 100 in any one hour), 25 for each trophy, 50 for each mastery medal, 20 for each rank-up, 5,000 for reaching Dark Matter on each journey, 20,000 for reaching the ModuPro and 30,000 for reaching the Loupes (if you got there before these were added, they're already in your balance) and 1,000 for each survey you answer and your first check-in for each exam (that reward's 1,000 XP doesn't add crowns of its own) and as many crowns as XP for every bonus (next entry). There is no daily limit on XP or crowns. Spending them never lowers your XP or your rank. Your balance is on the dashboard's You card, on a hub's Today card (on Home and beside the Question Bank, with the crowns you've earned today under it) and on the shop's counter. The shop is on the dashboard's You card (the Shop button), in every hub under More, and from Timmy's place (its Shop button). Today's picks (four pieces, new at midnight Central time), This week (three, new every Monday), the seasons' sets while they're on, a "Back for today" shelf on two throwback days a month, and the snacks and boosts, always. Tap anything for a closer look; Buy asks once more, with your balance after. Outfits, homes, scenes, yard pieces and the home's upgrades are yours for good: "Put it on" or "Place it" takes you to the customizer. Year-round collections: six sets of things that belong together, each a home, a scene, three outfits and three yard pieces: Dino valley (a stone-age den, a volcano valley, a T. rex skeleton with all its teeth), Moon base (a dome on the Moon with the Earth in the sky, a rocket on its pad, a jetpack), Coral reef (a conch shell house under the sea, a giant clam, a mer-tail), Desert ranch (an adobe ranch house, red rocks, a windmill, a cowboy hat), Retro arcade (an arcade hall in pixel hills, a giant claw machine, pixel shades) and Rock show (a record shop, a festival field, a drum kit, an electric guitar). They aren't limited like a season's set: they come up in Today's picks and This week all year, the rarer pieces less often, and sit under their own Collections tab when you customize. Six more paint colors too: coral, sage, sand, rose, slate and teal. Rarity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic and Legendary, each with its own frame. The rarer a piece, the less often it's on a shelf. Today's showcase is the rarest piece on sale that you don't own yet. Snacks for Timmy: an apple (+10 HP), a cheese cube (+15), floss (+25) and a fluoride rinse (+40), one of each a day, and not while he's at 100 HP. He eats it at once. Studying still heals him too. Double XP boosts: 150 crowns for one hour, 400 for three. A boost starts when you buy it; bought while double XP is already on (a medal's 24 hours or another boost), it starts when that ends, so none of it is wasted, and the shop tells you when before you buy. Win a medal while one is running and the rest of it waits for the medal's 24 hours to end. The 2x shows on your rank.

Bonuses: XP and crowns: Each of these pays as many crowns as XP, and your balance goes up the moment it's paid (a gold "+ crowns" pops under your rank). The cards say what they pay before you start: Timmy Time ("Up to +580 XP and 340 crowns"), a lecture's Mark as read, the arcade, the daily goal, Visit someone random and the name in Settings. Your daily ring: 5 a question of your daily goal (100 for a goal of 20), once a day in each hub, when the ring is full. A Plaque Boss: your share of 500, by how much of its health you took off. A lecture read to the end: 50, once per lecture. Scrolling straight to the bottom doesn't count: it pays after about as long as the notes take to read (at least a minute), and only while you're on the page. Right in a row: 25 at 10, 100 at 25 and 250 at 50 (a fourth try at the same question that day, a self-graded card or a too-fast answer doesn't add to the run). Your day streak: 100 at 3 days, 300 at 7, 700 at 14, 1,500 at 30, 3,000 at 60 and 5,000 at 100. Launching a tactical nuke: 10,000, once for every 100 right in a row. Breaking the class's all-time streak record (the longest run of right answers in a row, past 100): 20,000, once per run. Trophies: 200 for each one you win from now on. Mastery medals: 250, 500, 750 and 1,000 for Bronze to Crown. The arcade: 100 for your first game of the day, 50 for a personal best and 250 for a new high score in the hub (once a day for each game). Visiting a classmate's Timmy: 50, once a day. Picking your leaderboard name: 500, once. A report you sent that gets fixed: 100 XP and now 100 crowns too. Timmy Time: 10 XP a minute heard as before, and 100 XP and 100 crowns for finishing the episode. Finishing a collection: 1,000, once for each one (the Collections entry, next).

Collections: Collections shows everything you can collect in Timmy's shop and how far you've got with each: every holiday and season's set (Thanksgiving, the winter holidays, New Year and the rest, Halloween 2026's gift too), the six year-round collections (Dino valley to Rock show) and the ten rare costumes. Each is a card with a bar ("3 of 8"), its pieces in their rarity's colors (yours in color with a gold tick, the rest gray, with their price when you hold or tap one) and when it's in the shop; the sets on sale now come first. Open it from the dashboard's You card (next to Timmy's shop), from Timmy's place (the Collections button under Customize and Shop) or in a hub under More → Timmy's place → Your collections. Finish one for +1,000 XP and 1,000 crowns, once for each collection. Buy its last piece and the shop pays it on the spot; a collection you'd already finished before this shows a Claim button. Halloween 2026's set was a gift to everyone, so it's finished from the start and pays no bonus, and rank pieces aren't a collection: they come with your rank.

Visiting: Tap anyone on the dashboard's leaderboard (Ranks or Study streaks, the top three on the stage too) to fly over through the clouds to their Timmy's place: their home, scene and yard, what their Timmy is wearing, their rank's statue and their hub medals, under their leaderboard name. Tap their Timmy and he waves; the things around the place do what they do at yours. Your own row opens your own place. From a hub's arcade: on a game's class board (its game-over card), a classmate's name is underlined with dots; tap it to visit their place, and closing it brings you back to the board. Visit someone random (under the leaderboard) rolls the die and takes you to anyone in the class who has decorated their place, on the leaderboard or not (never your own). Next rolls again, the back arrow returns to the places you've been, and you meet everyone once before anyone comes round twice. Top ten: visiting someone in the leaderboard's top ten shows their number next to their name: gold for #1, silver for #2, bronze for #3. Visiting from the leaderboard, the arrows on either side take you to the next or the last place on the board. Back to mine brings you home. What a visitor sees, and doesn't: only the place. Never your HP, XP as a number, your streak, your answers, your Shiny Gold Crowns, what you own beyond what's out, or when you did anything. Nobody can change your place but you, and there's no list of who visited. Everyone on a board can be visited (there's no switch to turn it off).
His trophies: Pearly Whites for getting him to 100 HP (a Timmy who starts at 100 has to slip below it first and come back); Full Recovery for bringing him from 0 back to 100.

sections.title: Easter eggs
items: None of them appear during a mock exam. Settings → Extras switches them off: the Golden Probe, Tooth Fairy, Plaque Boss and the nuke each have their own switch, Hidden secrets covers the rest, and All off turns everything off at once. Magic words can be typed anywhere on a hub page (not in a text box), or into the hub's Search box on a phone.

sections.title: Holidays and seasons
items: Dates are Central time and switch on by themselves. During a holiday the confetti changes, every boss wears a costume and takes a seasonal name, Timmy has a whole set of holiday greetings, cheers and jokes (never the same one twice in a row), his place puts out its holiday props, and the magic word works. In the fall weeks between holidays he has autumn lines too. Timmy no longer dresses himself for a holiday: he wears what you put on him, and the holiday looks are in the shop's seasonal sets.
